author: Unsigned statement (corpus lists General Conference of SDA)
work: Fundamental Principles of Seventh-day Adventists, 1889 Year Book, p. 147, Principle I
text: I. That there is one God, a personal, spiritual being, … unchangeable, and everywhere present by his representative, the Holy Spirit. Psalm 139:7.
note: Principle I: God is “everywhere present by his representative, the Holy Spirit” (Psalm 139:7).

author: Unsigned statement (corpus lists General Conference of SDA)
work: Fundamental Principles of Seventh-day Adventists, 1889 Year Book, p. 150, Principle XVII
text: XVII. That as the natural or carnal heart is at enmity with God and his law, this enmity can be subdued only by a radical transformation of the affections, the exchange of unholy for holy principles; that this transformation follows repentance and faith, is the special work of the Holy Spirit, and constitutes regeneration, or conversion.
note: Principle XVII: the transformation of the heart “is the special work of the Holy Spirit, and constitutes regeneration, or conversion.”

author: Unsigned statement (corpus lists General Conference of SDA)
work: Fundamental Principles of Seventh-day Adventists, 1889 Year Book, p. 150, Principle XIX
text: … that, in specifying the various channels of its operation, that Spirit has simply made provision for its own existence and presence with the people of God to the end of time, to lead to an understanding of that word which it had inspired, to convince of sin, and to work a transformation in the heart and life; and that those who deny to the Spirit its place and operation, do plainly deny that part of the Bible which assigns to it this work and position.
note: Principle XIX names the Spirit’s work (understanding of “that word which it had inspired,” conviction of sin, transformation of heart and life) and refers to the Spirit as “it”/“its.”

author: James White
work: “Personality of God,” unsigned editorial, Advent Review and Sabbath Herald, June 18, 1861 (the same text is signed “J. W.” in the tract Personality of God, PERGO 6.1)
text: God is everywhere by virtue of his Spirit, which is his representative, and is manifested wherever he pleases, as will be seen by the very words the objector claims, referred to above. Verses 7-10. “Whither shall I go from thy Spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence? …
note: James White, 1861: God is everywhere “by virtue of his Spirit, which is his representative” — the idea Principle I states in 1872 and 1889.

author: J. H. Waggoner
text: We are not only willing but anxious to leave it just where the word of God leaves it. From it we learn that the Spirit of God is that awful and mysterious power which proceeds from the throne of the universe, and which is the efficient actor of the work of creation and of redemption.
note: J. H. Waggoner, 1877: having declined to enter the question of the Spirit’s personality (SGOM 8.2), he calls the Spirit “that awful and mysterious power which proceeds from the throne of the universe,” “the efficient actor” in creation and redemption.

author: Uriah Smith
text: And then the Holy Spirit (by an infirmity of translation called .. the Holy Ghost”), the Spirit of God, the Spirit of Christ, the divine afflatus and medium of their power, representative of them both (Psalm 139:7), was in existence also.
note: Uriah Smith, 1898: the Holy Spirit is “the Spirit of God, the Spirit of Christ, the divine afflatus and medium of their power, representative of them both.”

author: Ellen G. White
text: The Holy Spirit is Christ’s representative, but divested of the personality of humanity, and independent thereof. Cumbered with humanity, Christ could not be in every place personally. Therefore it was for their interest that He should go to the Father, and send the Spirit to be His successor on earth. … By the Spirit the Saviour would be accessible to all.
note: EGW, 1898: “The Holy Spirit is Christ’s representative, but divested of the personality of humanity”; Christ sends the Spirit as “His successor on earth” so that he is “accessible to all.”

author: Ellen G. White
text: The Spirit was to be given as a regenerating agent, and without this the sacrifice of Christ would have been of no avail. … Sin could be resisted and overcome only through the mighty agency of the Third Person of the Godhead, who would come with no modified energy, but in the fullness of divine power. It is the Spirit that makes effectual what has been wrought out by the world’s Redeemer. It is by the Spirit that the heart is made pure.
note: EGW, 1898: the Spirit is “a regenerating agent” and “the Third Person of the Godhead,” who comes “in the fullness of divine power.”

author: Ellen G. White
text: The nature of the Holy Spirit is a mystery. Men cannot explain it, because the Lord has not revealed it to them. Men having fanciful views may bring together passages of Scripture and put a human construction on them, but the acceptance of these views will not strengthen the church. Regarding such mysteries, which are too deep for human understanding, silence is golden.
note: EGW, 1911: “The nature of the Holy Spirit is a mystery”; human constructions of it “will not strengthen the church”; “silence is golden.” (John 15:26; 16:13 are cited in the preceding paragraph, AA 51.3.)
